title: The Bakery of Junebug Creek
premise: Lior Thackeray inherits Thackeray Vineyards along with a mountain of debt and a family that treats love like a ledger entry. To survive the Junebug Creek centennial reunion without pitying relatives or a scheming cousin circling the estate, Lior hires Wren Okafor, a baker whose festival stall is the town's beating heart, to pose as their partner for one weekend. The fake courtship curdles into something real just as Lior discovers the family debt was manufactured by an uncle angling to seize the vineyard — and that exposing him means betraying the mother who helped bury the truth. At the harvest festival's final night, Lior must choose between protecting the family name and speaking the sentence rehearsed for ten years: 'I loved you then, and I never stopped.' They say it — to Wren, not to the family — choosing truth over loyalty, and the two of them open a bakery-and-vineyard on the ruins of the old lie.
about_author: Isandro Blackwood is the pen name of a former sommelier who traded cellar logs for manuscripts after a decade of watching families negotiate love over wine. They write romances set in small towns where every recipe hides a secret, and they still can't resist a hero who mistakes duty for destiny.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Returning to Junebug Creek for the reading of the will, Lior inherits a vineyard mortgaged to its trellises and a letter from their late father demanding they 'settle the family account.' The emotional beat is grief sharpened into resentment as Lior vows the heart stays locked.

chapters.title: The Baker at Stall Nine
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Okafor runs the festival's most beloved stall, feeding the town gossip alongside peach hand pies. When Lior storms past looking like a storm cloud in linen, Wren offers a tart and unsolicited advice. The beat: reluctant fascination between two people who pride themselves on self-sufficiency.

chapters.title: A Reunion Requires a Plus-One
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Cousin Marisol announces she's contesting the will, and Aunt Bev begins matchmaking Lior with a banker's son. Cornered, Lior tracks down Wren with an absurd offer: paid companionship for three reunion weekends. The beat: humiliation braided with desperation.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions of the Heart
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren needs a new oven and a lawyer for her lease; Lior's money solves both. She agrees but drafts rules: no real feelings, no lies about the past. The beat: wary contract-signing where both pretend the handshake didn't linger.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner, Unrehearsed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The first staged appearance goes sideways when Lior's mother, Odette, recognizes something familiar in how Wren laughs. A toast nearly exposes Lior's childhood secret. The beat: the fake romance works too well, and being believed feels dangerously like being seen.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Inventorying the wine cellar, Lior finds ledgers showing payments to a shell company — Uncle Ambrose's consulting firm — draining the vineyard for years. The beat: suspicion planted; loyalty to family begins to crack against the first hard fact.

chapters.title: Flour on Your Collar
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren catches Lior sleeping in the bakery at dawn after fleeing a family fight, flour-dusted and defeated. She teaches them to knead dough; Lior teaches her why they flinch at the word 'home.' The beat: intimacy disguised as instruction.

chapters.title: The Second Weekend
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Reunion weekend two: a boat race forces genuine teamwork, and Marisol corners Wren with questions about Lior's decade away. Wren improvises a tender lie about 'the accident' — inventing a history neither confirmed. The beat: the fiction deepens beyond either author's control.

chapters.title: Ambrose Offers a Deal
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Uncle Ambrose proposes buying the vineyard 'generously,' erasing the debt if Lior signs by festival's end. He mentions Odette's signature is already on older papers. The beat: power revealed as leverage; Lior realizes the trap has been closing for years.

chapters.title: Ten Years of One Sentence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds a worn notebook in Lior's truck: a single sentence, rewritten across a decade of dates, addressed to no one yet. She doesn't read it aloud, but she stops pretending this arrangement is simple. The beat: longing acknowledged in silence.

chapters.title: Odette's Garden
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Confronting Odette about the ledgers, Lior learns she co-signed the shell payments to protect the family from a scandal involving Lior's late father. Loyalty versus truth becomes literal: expose Ambrose, and expose Mother too. The beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rain strands them in the tasting room; almost-kiss interrupted by Marisol's arrival with a lawyer's letter challenging the will. Lior pulls Wren behind the bar, kissing her for the audience — except no one is watching anymore. The beat: the fake collapses mid-performance.

chapters.title: Rules We Broke
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren breaks rule one by spending the night — talking, not touching — while Lior finally reads her the sentence's first draft from ten years ago, written to someone who left. The beat: vulnerability exchanged like currency neither can take back.

chapters.title: Marisol's Leverage
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Marisol reveals she knows Wren was hired, offering silence in exchange for Lior dropping the will contest — which would hand Ambrose the vineyard. The beat: blackmail forcing Lior to weigh Wren's heart against the family estate.

chapters.title: The Town That Talks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Gossip reaches the bakery: Wren is 'for sale.' Regulars turn cold; her lease lawyer warns the landlord got a call from Ambrose. The beat: collateral damage — loving Lior is starting to cost Wren everything she built alone.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the eve of the centennial festival, Lior tells Wren the truth about everything: the ledgers, Odette, the deal, the blackmail. Wren's answer isn't comfort — it's a plan, and a demand: no more rehearsed sentences, only spoken ones. The beat: alliance forged in honesty.

chapters.title: The Centennial Toast
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the festival's opening ceremony, Ambrose publicly toasts the family legacy while privately giving Lior until midnight to sign. Lior stands before the whole town holding the ledger pages, mouth dry, Wren's eyes steady in the crowd. The beat: the cliff edge.

chapters.title: Truth at Midnight
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. Before the crowd, Lior exposes the shell company, naming Ambrose — and, voice breaking, admits Odette's part, asking forgiveness rather than permission. Ambrose detonates the Wren-was-hired bomb. The beat: truth as detonation; every relationship on the table burns.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Humiliated and hurt, Wren turns to leave — and Lior abandons the stage, the family, the signing deadline, to say it in front of everyone: 'I loved you then, and I never stopped' — first to the ghost of the past, then, kneeling in pie crumbs, to Wren. The beat: catharsis; the rehearsed decade ends.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Ash
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Fallout: Ambrose arrested, Odette estranged but reachable, Marisol's contest settled when the real will surfaces — leaving Lior the vineyard free of debt. But Wren has gone quiet, needing time. The beat: victory hollowed by uncertainty.

chapters.title: What Wren Decided
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wrestles with whether love built on a contract can be trusted, rereading the notebook's ten years of drafts. Her grandmother's recipe box yields the answer: some things you don't inherit, you make. The beat: choice reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Bakery of Junebug Creek
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Spring: the vineyard's tasting room now shares walls with Wren's bakery, sign painted by townsfolk who once gossiped. Odette visits; Lior lets her in slowly. Final image: two names on one door, no contracts anywhere. The beat: love chosen daily, freely, home made at last.
